entries.name: Woodland BDU
entries.summary: Four-color woodland camouflage battle dress uniform. The Army field uniform from the early 1980s until the ACU.
facts: Adopted in 1981 as the Battle Dress Uniform (BDU)
Replaced by the ACU, fielded starting in 2005
A six-color desert version was issued for desert operations

variants.label: Woodland BDU (four-color)
variants.note: The standard green, brown, and black pattern.

entries.name: Pinks and greens
entries.summary: WWII-era officer service uniform: pink-toned trousers with a dark green coat. Brought back in modern form as the Army Green Service Uniform.
facts: Pink-toned trousers with a dark olive-green coat
Officer combination in World War II
The modern Army Green Service Uniform revives the look
entries.remember: Pinks on the legs, greens on the coat.

variants.label: Army Green Service Uniform
variants.note: The modern revival of the look.

entries.name: Army Blue dress uniform
entries.summary: Dark blue formal uniform worn for formal and ceremonial occasions.
facts: Service stripes and overseas service bars go on the sleeves
Ribbons and badges go above the left pocket
entries.remember: Blue is for dress, green is for service.

entries.name: Army Commendation Medal
entries.summary: Army award for heroism, meritorious achievement, or meritorious service.
facts: Began in 1945 as the Army Commendation Ribbon
Became the Army Commendation Medal in 1960

attachments.name: Devices
attachments.note: Devices that can be pinned on the ribbon.

variants.label: V device
variants.note: Shows the award was earned for valor.

entries.name: Oak leaf cluster
entries.summary: Small metal device pinned on a ribbon to show additional awards of the same medal.
facts: Bronze oak leaf cluster: one additional award
Silver oak leaf cluster: five additional awards
Navy and Marine Corps use stars instead
entries.remember: Oak leaves for Army and Air Force, stars for Navy and Marines.

entries.name: V device
entries.summary: Small bronze letter V added to a ribbon to show the award was earned for valor.
facts: Worn centered on the ribbon
Only authorized awards can carry it

entries.name: Sharpshooter badge
entries.summary: Middle marksmanship qualification badge, above Marksman and below Expert. Weapon bars hang underneath.
facts: Three levels: Marksman, Sharpshooter, Expert
A bar for each weapon type hangs from the badge
Comes in a polished (shiny) finish and a subdued (non-shiny) finish

attachments.name: Qualification bars
attachments.note: Bar names and the full bar list still need to be checked.

entries.name: Parachutist badge
entries.summary: Army jump badge in three levels: Basic, Senior, and Master.
facts: Three levels: Basic, Senior, Master
Combat jump stars mark combat jumps
entries.remember: Basic, Senior, Master: the badge adds a star, then a wreath.

entries.name: Service stripes and overseas service
entries.summary: Sleeve marks that show length of service and time overseas. Each branch has its own rules.
facts: Army dress service stripe: one per three years of service
Overseas service bar: one per six months overseas
WWI overseas service chevron: one per six months overseas
entries.remember: Stripes count years, bars and chevrons count overseas time.

variants.label: Overseas service chevron
variants.note: One chevron per six months overseas. Color to verify.

variants.label: Service stripe
variants.note: One stripe per three years. Color per uniform to verify.

variants.label: Overseas service bar
variants.note: One bar per six months overseas. Color per uniform to verify.

entries.name: Ranger tab
entries.summary: Tab worn above the unit patch by Ranger School graduates.
facts: Worn above the unit shoulder patch
Earlier eras and colors still need to be added

variants.label: Ranger tab
variants.note: Colors still need to be checked.

entries.name: Airborne tab
entries.summary: Tab worn above the unit patch by airborne-qualified soldiers.
facts: Worn above the unit shoulder patch
Era colors still need to be added

entries.name: Sergeant (E-5)
entries.summary: Army enlisted rank insignia, shown per uniform and per gender.
facts: Insignia color changes with the uniform
Each variant lists the uniform it belongs to
